entity.name: Frédéric Chopin
entity.description: The pianist who redefined what a piano could say. Polish-born composer who wrote almost exclusively for solo piano, producing mazurkas, nocturnes, and ballades that expanded the instrument's emotional and technical range. He gave only 30 public concerts in his life, preferring intimate salons. Died in Paris at 39, likely of tuberculosis.

story.name: Frédéric Chopin
story.description: A child prodigy leaves Warsaw weeks before revolution, conquers Parisian salons, writes masterpieces in a Mallorcan monastery while battling illness, and dies at 39. The life of Romantic piano's greatest voice.

moments.name: Frédéric Chopin Is Born in a Village 46 Kilometers West of Warsaw
moments.subtitle: The son of a French emigrant and a Polish mother who will never return to his homeland
moments.description: On March 1, 1810, Frédéric François Chopin was born in Żelazowa Wola, a small village in the Duchy of Warsaw, to Nicolas Chopin, a French emigrant, and Justyna Krzyżanowska. The family moved to Warsaw six months later, where Chopin's father taught French at the Warsaw Lyceum. By age seven, the child was giving public concerts and composing polonaises. His final conservatory report in 1829 read simply: "exceptional talent, musical genius." Chopin would leave Poland at 20 and never return, yet Polish folk music pervaded every note he wrote.

moments.name: Chopin Gives a Farewell Concert in Warsaw Before Leaving Poland Forever
moments.subtitle: He exchanges rings with a singer he never spoke his feelings to, then departs weeks before an uprising
moments.description: In October 1830, 20-year-old Frédéric Chopin performed his Piano Concerto No. 1 at the National Theatre in Warsaw in what would be his final concert on Polish soil. The soprano Konstancja Gładkowska, who Chopin had secretly adored for over a year, sang a Rossini aria. The two exchanged rings afterward, though Chopin had never directly confessed his feelings. Less than a month later, the November Uprising against Russian rule erupted. Chopin, already en route to Vienna, would never return to Poland. His longing for his homeland shaped decades of mazurkas and polonaises.

moments.name: Chopin Settles in Paris and Conquers the City's Most Elite Salons
moments.subtitle: A 21-year-old exile who will give only 30 public concerts in his entire career
moments.description: In September 1831, 21-year-old Frédéric Chopin arrived in Paris after fleeing the political turmoil in Poland. He quickly gained entry to the city's most prestigious salons, befriending Franz Liszt and earning admiration from Robert Schumann, who famously declared upon hearing Chopin's Variations on "Là ci darem la mano": "Hats off, gentlemen, a genius!" Rather than pursuing a public concert career, Chopin preferred intimate salon performances and supported himself by teaching piano to aristocratic students. Paris remained his home for the rest of his life.

moments.name: Chopin Spends a Miserable Winter in Mallorca That Produces Some of His Greatest Works
moments.subtitle: Rain, illness, and a hostile village somehow yield the 24 Preludes
moments.description: In November 1838, Frédéric Chopin traveled to Mallorca with the French writer George Sand and her children, hoping the Mediterranean climate would improve his deteriorating health. Instead, they were evicted from their villa when locals learned of Chopin's illness, and retreated to an abandoned Carthusian monastery in Valldemossa. Rain leaked through the walls, Chopin's piano arrived late, and his coughing worsened. Yet during this miserable winter of 1838-39, Chopin completed his 24 Preludes, Op. 28, and several other major works. It proved one of his most productive periods despite the suffering.
moments.address: Real Cartuja de Valldemossa, Mallorca, Spain

moments.name: Chopin Dies in Paris at 39 After Requesting Mozart's Requiem at His Funeral
moments.subtitle: His heart is smuggled to Warsaw in a jar of cognac, where it remains today
moments.description: On October 17, 1849, Frédéric Chopin died at 12 Place Vendôme in Paris at the age of 39, likely of tuberculosis that had plagued him for years. In his final days, he was attended by his sister Ludwika, who had traveled from Warsaw. Chopin requested that Mozart's Requiem be performed at his funeral, held at the Madeleine church on October 30. Per his wishes, his body was buried at Père Lachaise Cemetery in Paris, but his heart was removed and smuggled by his sister to Warsaw, where it remains preserved in a pillar of the Holy Cross Church to this day.
